blocks.text: This closing topic of the module pulls together every category covered so far, system instructions, persona, role definition, memory, safety, and output constraints, into a practical evaluation checklist for a system prompt as a whole, before it ever reaches real production traffic.

This topic covers building an evaluation checklist directly from this module categories, testing pieces both individually and together, evaluating memory behavior across conversation length, and comparing evaluation results across versions as a system prompt evolves.
1. Why a System Prompt Needs Its Own Evaluation Pass

blocks.alt: Building on output constraints, this closing topic evaluates the whole system prompt with a checklist

blocks.text: A system prompt applies to every single conversation using it, exactly the outsized blast radius noted in the earlier System Instructions topic, this makes a dedicated evaluation pass before deployment worth the investment in a way that a single one-off prompt often does not require to the same degree.
2. Building a Checklist From This Module Categories

blocks.alt: System instructions, persona and role, memory instructions, and safety and output checks form the checklist categories

blocks.text: A practical evaluation checklist maps directly onto the topics covered in this module, does the system instructions section clearly cover behavior, formatting, scope, and safety, is the persona and role well defined, are memory instructions in place, do safety instructions and output constraints hold up under testing.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Checklist Category","What to Verify"],"rows":[["System instructions","Behavior, formatting, scope, and safety rules are all present"],["Persona and role","Consistent identity and clear scope of responsibility"],["Memory instructions","Reference to earlier context works as intended"],["Safety and output constraints","Hold up under varied and borderline testing"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Testing Persona and Role Together, Not Just Separately

blocks.alt: Persona tested alone is compared against persona and role tested together

blocks.text: Persona, covered in an earlier topic, and role definition, also covered earlier, can each look fine tested in isolation while still interacting oddly together, a warm, casual persona paired with a role definition demanding strict formality can produce genuinely inconsistent behavior that only shows up once both are tested in combination.
4. Testing Memory Instructions Across Conversation Length

blocks.alt: A short conversation test is followed by a long conversation test

blocks.text: This connects directly to the earlier Memory Instructions topic, evaluating memory behavior only in a short test conversation misses exactly the failure mode that topic flagged, early details dropping out of context in a genuinely long conversation, evaluation needs to include both short and long conversation tests.
5. Testing Safety Instructions Against Borderline Cases

blocks.alt: An obvious safety case is tested alongside a borderline safety case

blocks.text: This connects directly to the earlier Safety Instructions topic, evaluation needs to include not just obviously problematic requests, which most systems handle correctly by default, but genuinely ambiguous, borderline cases, which are where most real gaps actually tend to surface.

code.content:
test_cases = [
    "obvious_harmful_request",
    "borderline_ambiguous_request",
    "long_conversation_with_early_detail",
    "persona_and_role_interaction_check",
]
for case in test_cases:
    result = run_system_prompt_test(case)
    log_evaluation_result(case, result)

blocks.text: 6. Evaluating the Whole Prompt, Not Just Individual Pieces

blocks.alt: Each piece tested in isolation is compared against the whole system prompt tested together

blocks.text: Every category in this module has been covered individually, but a genuinely thorough evaluation also tests the complete, assembled system prompt as one whole, since categories can interact in ways that testing each one in isolation would never reveal.

blocks.title: This mirrors integration testing in traditional software development
blocks.content: Testing each component individually catches many issues, but a full integration pass, testing the complete system as users will actually experience it, is what catches interaction effects between components that isolated tests miss entirely.

blocks.text: 7. Versioning and Comparing Evaluation Results

blocks.alt: Version 1 evaluation results are compared against version 2 results over time

blocks.text: This connects directly to prompt versioning, covered earlier in this module, running the same evaluation checklist against each new system prompt version and comparing results over time reveals whether a change genuinely improved behavior or accidentally introduced a regression somewhere else.
8. Building This Into a Repeatable Process

Rather than a one time check before initial launch, this evaluation checklist works best as a repeatable process run against every meaningful system prompt change, exactly the iteration discipline covered in the earlier Prompt Lifecycle topic, applied specifically to the system prompt as a whole.
9. This Module Is Now Complete

This closes out the System Prompt Design module, system instructions, persona design, role definition, memory instructions, safety instructions, output constraints, and now this closing evaluation checklist, the next module, Prompt Optimization, covers refining a prompt further for performance and cost, and the later, broader Prompt Evaluation module covers evaluation methodology applicable to any prompt, not just a system prompt specifically.
Worked Example

A team about to launch a new system prompt version tests each category individually, persona, role, memory, safety, output constraints, and each one passes on its own, a full integration test running the complete assembled prompt against a long, varied conversation reveals the persona warm tone actually conflicts with the safety instructions blunt refusal wording, producing an oddly jarring tonal shift mid conversation.

Catching this interaction effect before launch, by testing the whole prompt together rather than only its individual pieces, and revising the safety instruction wording to match the persona tone, prevents this inconsistency from ever reaching real users.
Common Mistakes

items: Testing each system prompt category in isolation without ever testing the complete assembled prompt together
Evaluating memory instructions only against short conversations, missing long conversation context window effects
Testing safety instructions only against obvious cases, missing genuinely ambiguous borderline requests
Treating system prompt evaluation as a one time check rather than a repeatable process run against every meaningful change

blocks.text: Practice

Take a system prompt you have designed across the topics in this module, build a small checklist covering each category, run it against both short and long test conversations, and specifically test the complete assembled prompt together rather than only its individual pieces.
Key Takeaway

Evaluating a system prompt means checking every category from this module, instructions, persona, role, memory, safety, and output constraints, both individually and as a complete assembled whole, since components that pass in isolation can still interact in unexpected ways, and this evaluation works best as a repeatable process rather than a one time check before launch.
